A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, including the supplementary experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports an original 2,976-participant user study, empirical comparisons of consistency metrics, ensemble experiments, and an appendix pilot study.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and additionally reports inter-rater agreement, runtime measurements, feature-selection frequencies, and example-level discrepancies.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same consistency aggregation and linear ensemble of 16 features derived from four token metrics and four aggregations. Sequential Feature Selection remains the selection procedure; its revised explanation and citation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CoQA and filtered English-language LMSYS prompts using US adult Prolific participants. The example prompts added in Appendix A.4 illustrate retained coverage rather than introduce another dataset or task.

E2.justification: The response-pair comparisons retain Bert, BLEU, Rouge, and USE; response-to-set and prompt comparisons additionally retain Semantic Entropy. The new timing comparison reuses selected existing comparators without changing membership in the retained comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds a runtime evaluation using the same GPU for 1,000 responses to 100 prompts, plus ensemble-training timing under cross-validation. The original model configurations, response sampling, user-study procedures, and consistency evaluation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds analysis of which features SFS selects most frequently (Table 5), computational efficiency measurements, and four examples of human–USE discrepancies (Appendix A.4, Table 7). The existing feature-count sensitivity analysis, identical-response pilot, and dataset-specific comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 newly reports Krippendorff's alpha of 0.72 after removing extreme ratings. Both versions already describe 100 repetitions per feature-count setting, totaling 1,600 SFS runs with 10-fold cross-validation, and retain the same Figure 5 boxplots.

E6.justification: The principal consistency scores remain unchanged. New results include maximum entropy selected 1,569 times and summed log probability 1,384 times; evaluation times of 0.0044 seconds for the ensemble versus 23 seconds for USE; and a dessert-recipe prompt with human consistency 0.30 versus USE 0.63. These supplement existing findings rather than demonstrate improved performance between versions.

T1.justification: The token-entropy and DLR definitions and consistency equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v3 introduces no new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The conclusion modestly broadens its recommendation for human validation from consistency-metric revisions to research using these metrics for downstream tasks. The main claims about human–metric mismatch, ensemble performance, and avoiding resampling remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4 now qualifies the human-rating baseline as the closest representation of ground truth, and Section 4.2 characterizes measured agreement as moderate. The explanation proposed for the CoQA–LMSYS gap and limitations concerning black-box models, text length, and sample size remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an artifact-distribution section providing an OSF DOI for project code, anonymized participant data, and analysis results, substantially expanding reproducibility information beyond v1's tool links. It also discloses $1 participant compensation, median completion time, and ensemble training and evaluation times. The PDFs establish the access statement, not the external artifacts' contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds Krippendorff (2011), Marzi et al. (2024), and Rückstieß et al. (2011), and removes Balabanov and Linander (2024). Scikit-learn documentation remains linked through a footnote. These are limited citation changes without substantial repositioning.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, methods, results, and discussion, refining grammar, terminology, and explanations of the comparison hierarchy. Some user-study information is reorganized, and artifact-distribution and example-prompt sections are added, although the main section sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The results presentation is substantially revised: Figure 2 separates correlation and MSE panels with narrower scales and a relocated legend; Figure 3 narrows its axis and adds a reference line. New Tables 5 and 7 display feature frequencies and example discrepancies. Figures 5 and 6 retain their content after relocation.

improvement.justification: v3 better supports the human baseline with agreement reporting and the efficiency claim with measured runtimes. Feature-selection details, discrepancy examples, clearer prose, and artifact-access information improve transparency. The gains remain limited: principal results and coverage are unchanged, and the single-response validation gap and inconsistent unique-response-pair counts remain unresolved.
